questions.question: State the multiplication theorem of probability if events are independent. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• If two events A and B are independent, then the probability of both events occurring
  • together (i.e., the intersection of A and B) is the product of their individual probabilities.
  • P(A∩B) = P(A)×P(B)

questions.question: Explain the meaning and significance of the concept of correlation? Does it always signify cause and effect relationship between two variables? How is the coefficient of correlation interpreted? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Correlation measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two
  • variables, indicating how they move together (e.g., height and weight). Its significance lies
  • in identifying associations for prediction, decision -making, and modeling, with a range
  • between -1 and +1.
  • No, correlation does not always signify a cause -and-effect relationship. While correlated
  • variables move together, this does not mean one causes the other to change.. The coefficient
  • of correlation ranges from -1 to +1:
  • +1 indicates a perfect positive linear relationship,
  • -1 indicates a perfect negative linear relationship,
  • 0 indicates no linear relationship.

questions.question: A portfolio manager is selecting 4 stocks to add to a high-growth fund from a shortlist of 10 potential companies. The shortlist consists of: 3 Banking Stocks, 4 IT Stocks, 2 Pharma Stocks and 1 Auto Stock If the 4 stocks are selected at random, find the probability that: (i) The portfolio contains exactly one stock from each of the four sectors? (ii) The portfolio consists of the Auto stock and at least one Banking stock? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• (i) Exactly one stock from each sector = (3C1 X 4C1 X 2C1 X 1C1) / 10C4
  • = 24/210 = 4/35 or 0.114 ( 3 marks)
  • (ii) Auto stock and at least one banking stock =
  • If one auto stock is included (1C1= 1), number of selection for other stocks
  • = 9C3= 84
  • If banking stock is excluded in the remaining (Pharma + IT only)= 6C3= 20
  • At least one banking stock = 84- 20 = 64
  • Therefore, number of inclusion of auto stocks and at least one banking stock
  • = 64/210 = 32/105 = 0.3047 ( 4 marks)

questions.question: The annual profit (in ₹ crores) of MNO Ltd. is as follows: Year 2016 2017 2018 2019 2020 2021 2022 Profit 40 42 50 55 60 68 75 a) Fit a straight line trend by least squares method. b) Tabulate the trend values. c) Estimate the profit for 2023. / [CO3, CO5] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• The estimated profit for MNO Ltd. in 2023 is ₹79.57 crores.
  • To fit a straight line trend using the Least Squares Method, we use the equation:
  • Yc = a +bx ( y is profit, x is deviation from middle year 2019- Note- deviations can be taken
  • from any year)
  • Substituting in the equations , a =55.71 and b =5.96. (Ignore approximation differences)
  • (a) Trend equation is y= 55.71 + 5.96x
  • Year Profit (Y) x
  • (b) Trend
  • Values
  • 2016 40 -3 37.82
  • 2017 42 -2 43.79
  • 2018 50 -1 49.75
  • 2019 55 0 55.71
  • 2020 60 1 61.68
  • 2021 68 2 67.64
  • 2022 75 3 73.61
  • (c) For the Year 2023 the value of x = 4
  • Y= 55.714+5.96*4 = 79.57 or approximately 80 crores
